text:
Elaine: deploy-bot kicked off catalog enable for model-x-v2 on eu + na with fallback ordering set to [model-x-v2-quant, model-x-v1-quant, model-x-v1-full]. rolling window 2h starting now.

deploy-bot: STARTED rollout model-x-v2 2212345678 - canary: 1% traffic -> eu-west, na-east. Auto-rollback: enabled (error_rate>2% or latency>550ms).

canary-bot: canary metrics 5m: p95=480ms, p50=120ms, errors=0.7% overall. No regressions flagged.

David: seeing a small latency bump on eu-west spike at +80s, looks like batch sizing bumped from 16->32 on that pool. Anyone touching batching policy?

Carla: I pushed a conservative policy yesterday to reduce cold starts, might have increased per-request latency for short sequences. Reverting to target_batch=16 for eu-west makes sense for the canary.

Bjorn: +1 revert target_batch on the pool. Also we should pin the quant variant as higher priority until we finish perf vetting. Currently fallback ordering uses quant first which is fine, but catalog metadata incorrectly lists v1-full above v1-quant in some shards.

Alice: can we add a temporary override? Suggest config change:
```json
{"model_catalog": {"model-x": {"variants": ["model-x-v2-quant","model-x-v1-quant","model-x-v1-full"], "pin": "model-x-v2-quant"}}}
```
Will that be applied instantly?

deploy-bot: PATCH applied to catalog (override-id: oc-221234). Changes will propagate to routing in ~45s.

canary-bot: 2 checks later: eu-west p95=465ms, errors=0.5%, throughput stable. na-east p95=410ms. Canary traffic still 1%.

Elaine: good. Let's hold at 1% for 15m and then step to 10% if no regressions. Also schedule a rollback call if any region crosses error>1.5% for 3 consecutive checks.

David: FYI I opened a short postmortem note in #incidents if surge persists. For now looks contained.

Carla: I also updated the rollout notes in the release doc: added a step to verify fallback ordering via `rw-cli catalog get-priority model-x` before advancing traffic.

Bjorn: small operational ask — add a test that validates catalog priority order at deploy time. We had one shard with reversed ordering that caused a minority of traffic to hit v1-full.

Alice: on pinning — if we pin model-x-v2-quant please document the rollback pin too: `pin=null` to unpin or `pin=model-x-v1-quant` to revert. Saves time during an incident.

Elaine: noted. I'm keeping the change window open for 3h and will escalate to on-call if we need an immediate rollback. Thanks all. :raised_hands:

deploy-bot: ROLLOUT UPDATE: traffic stepped to 10% at 2212345850 after green checks. Canary ID c-221234. Monitoring for 30m.

canary-bot: 10m after step: global errors=0.6%, eu-west p95=470ms, na-east p95=420ms. No fail conditions met.

Elaine: continuing. If anyone sees anomalous traces tag them with `#model-x-rollout` and drop sample trace ids.

David: noted — pulling a few traces now, will post if anything looks bad.

Carla: prepared rollback playbook pinned in the doc: quick commands included. Snippet:
```bash
# rollback to v1-quant immediately
rw-cli catalog set-priority model-x --variants "model-x-v1-quant,model-x-v2-quant,model-x-v1-full"
# remove pin
rw-cli catalog unpin model-x
```

Bjorn: thanks. If we need to rollback we should also revert the batch policy change simultaneously to avoid a double-dip on latency.

Elaine: agreed. I'll keep this thread as the coordination thread for rollback decisions. If we hit thresholds we'll call SRE and shift to incident channel. :telephone_receiver:

deploy-bot: ROLLOUT COMPLETE: model-x-v2 at 10% for 30m without regressions. Next step scheduled: 50% at 2212349478 pending no alerts.
